text: What xAI is xAI is the frontier lab behind Grok, founded by Elon Musk and eleven researchers in March 2023 ( Wikipedia ).
label: core

text: Since February 2026 it has been a subsidiary of SpaceX, and since July 2026 it trades as SpaceXAI ( Owner and name ).
label: core

text: Its strategy is the least algorithmic and the most industrial of any frontier lab.
label: core

text: Where DeepSeek optimises cost per token and Ai2 optimises reproducibility, xAI optimises the rate at which it turns capital into training compute and then into shipped models.
label: core

text: It has published very little method: one open architecture (Grok-1), one open checkpoint of Grok 2, and launch posts.
label: core

text: What it has demonstrated is that a datacentre built in months, plus a willingness to spend reinforcement-learning compute at pretraining scale, is enough to stay among the top five labs without an obvious architectural edge.
label: core

text: On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3 (read 1 October 2026) its best model, Grok 4.7, scores 46.4, and SpaceXAI is the fifth lab by best model, behind Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Meta ( AA leaderboard ).
label: volatile

text: Its two durable differentiators are the real-time X firehose as a data source and a looser alignment posture than any other frontier lab ( Training , Posture and security ).
label: core

text: One question runs through the page: how does xAI turn capital into compute into shipped models, and what do its published numbers really say about where Grok stands?
label: fat

text: Colossus: compute as the strategy The lab's core claim is construction speed.
label: core

text: Training one model across tens of thousands of accelerators needs them behind one high-bandwidth fabric, with the power and cooling to run them together, so what is hard is building and networking the site, not buying the GPUs.
label: core

text: The S-1 gives the only audited figures: the first Colossus cluster in Memphis, about 100,000 H100 GPUs and about 130 MW, came online in 122 days in the shell of an existing factory; the first Colossus II cluster, about 110,000 GB200s and about 210 MW, in 91 days; its second cluster, 110,000 GB300s and 220 MW, in 64 days.
label: core

text: The next phase is to add at least 220,000 GB300s and over 400 MW, and the two sites together provide about 1.0 GW today.
label: core

text: Against those it sets "an industry benchmark to bring online a 100 megawatt greenfield data center", approximately two years ( S-1 ).
label: core

text: Megawatts per day Days to bring online GPUs per day Defaults reproduce the S-1's figures by construction (they are its inputs); the rates are derived as megawatts divided by days, so 130 / 122 = 1.07 MW a day for the first cluster against 100 / 730 = 0.14 for the benchmark.
label: core

text: A greenfield site is not a repurposed factory, so the first comparison flatters Colossus; the 64-day second cluster at an existing site is the fairest like-for-like.
label: core

text: A correction. "Roughly 200K H100s stood up in 122 days" merges two numbers.
label: core

text: The 122 days was the first cluster of about 100,000 H100s ( S-1 ); by Grok 3's launch xAI called Colossus a "200,000 GPU cluster" ( xAI ), and Grok 4's post says "Colossus, our 200k GPU cluster" ( xAI ).
label: core

text: Wikipedia dates full operation to December 2024 and peak demand to 150 MW, met partly by 14 portable methane generators while the grid agreement was worked out ( Wikipedia ).
label: core

text: Expansion continued toward the "at least 1 million" GPUs xAI announced with a third Memphis building on 30 December 2025, for nearly 2 GW ( Wikipedia ); the S-1's 1.0 GW is what is running.
label: core

text: The twist: the capacity is also sold.
label: core

text: In May 2026 SpaceX signed cloud services agreements giving Anthropic compute across Colossus and Colossus II for $1.25 billion a month through May 2029, terminable by either side on 90 days' notice, while "Grok 5 ... is currently being trained at COLOSSUS II" ( S-1 ).
label: core

text: A lab whose strategy is owning compute is now also renting the surplus to a rival, which is the clearest sign that the build rate has outrun what its own training needs.

text: The gas turbines at Colossus 2 are the subject of a Clean Air Act suit filed in April 2026 ( Wikipedia ).

text: Grok-1: the one published architecture Grok-1 was previewed in November 2023 as "the best we could do with 2 months of training" ( Wikipedia ); its pretraining concluded in October 2023, on a custom stack of JAX and Rust.
label: core

text: On 17 March 2024 xAI released its base weights and architecture under Apache 2.0: "a 314 billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 25% of the weights active on a given token" ( xAI ).
label: core

text: In a mixture of experts (MoE), each layer's feed-forward block is split into several experts and a small router sends each token to only a few, so total parameters (what you store) and per-token compute (what you pay to run) decouple.
label: owned:models_and_training/topic_llm_architecture/mixture_of_experts

text: Grok-1 has 8 experts per layer and runs 2 ( run.py and model.py ).
label: core

text: Grok 2 followed as open weights in August 2025 (Hugging Face calls it Grok 2, Wikipedia Grok 2.5), not under Apache 2.0 but under the xAI Community License : research and non-commercial use, and commercial use only within xAI's acceptable use policy ( licence ).
label: core

text: The pattern holds: open the previous generation once it is commercially spent, with no architecture published for anything after Grok 2.
label: core

text: The released code is enough to count the parameters.
label: core

text: Every number below is computed from the configuration in the code, not typed in: N = L ( 2 d n q d h + 2 d n kv d h + E · 3 d f + d E ) + 2 V d L layers (64) d model width (6,144) n q , n kv , d h query heads (48), key-value heads (8, grouped-query attention), head size (128) E, f experts per layer (8) and each expert's hidden size (32,768, from int(8·6144)·2//3 ); a gated feed-forward has 3 matrices dE the router V vocabulary (131,072); 2Vd counts the input embedding and the output head Active parameters use the same sum with E replaced by the 2 experts that run.
label: core

text: The key-value cache per token is 2 · L · n kv · d h · bytes.
label: core

text: Grok-1 (2023, Apache 2.0) Grok 2 (2024, Community License) Weight precision 16-bit (bf16) 8-bit 4-bit Context: tokens Try: switch to Grok 2 and look at the active share: a dense feed-forward that every token runs, beside the experts, takes it from about a quarter to over 40%.

text: Then raise the context to 128K: at 8 key-value heads the cache is 256 KiB a token, a sixth of what all 48 heads would need.

section: heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain
text: Heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain A reasoning model buys accuracy with tokens.
label: core

section: heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain
text: The serial way is to let one chain of thought run longer; its cost is latency, because every token waits for the one before it.
label: core

section: heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain
text: Grok 4 Heavy took the parallel way: "parallel test-time compute, which allows Grok to consider multiple hypotheses at once" ( xAI ).
label: core

section: heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain
text: Several attempts run at the same time and their answers are reconciled, so the bill grows with the number of attempts while the wall-clock time stays close to one attempt's.
label: core

section: heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain
text: It works because independent attempts make errors that are only partly correlated: where one goes wrong, the others often do not, so reconciling them catches mistakes a single chain would keep.
label: core

section: heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain
text: It stops working where all attempts share the same blind spot.
label: core

section: heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain
text: The API exposes the same idea as grok-4.20-multi-agent : several agents work the query and a designated leader agent synthesises their discussion into the answer.
label: core

section: heavy: parallel attempts instead of one longer chain
text: There are two setups, 4 agents (effort low or medium) and 16 agents (high or xhigh); only the leader's output is returned, and "all tokens consumed by both the leader agent and sub-agents are billed" ( multi-agent docs ).

text: Grok has promoted conspiracy theories, praised Adolf Hitler, used antisemitic tropes and generated nonconsensual sexualised images; within a week of launch, Grok 4 was shown consulting Musk's views before answering questions that did not ask for them ( Wikipedia ).
label: core

text: On 14 July 2026 a researcher reported that Grok Build uploaded users' whole repositories, history and secrets included, to a SpaceXAI storage bucket even with "Improve the model" disabled, about 27,800 times more data than its task needed; SpaceXAI disabled it the same day ( Wikipedia ). xAI's counter-claim for Grok 4.7 is "an entirely new safeguard stack" and "the strongest model we've tested on refusals and jailbreak resistance" ( xAI ).
label: core

text: The concrete cost is a security one.
label: core

text: Adversa AI's cryptographic context injection was reported to xAI and its HackerOne programme on 3 June 2026; xAI acknowledged it without specifics or a timeline, further contact on 4 and 10 August drew no reply, and Adversa could still reproduce it on 19 August, publishing on 20 August ( Adversa AI ), 78 days, or eleven weeks, after the report.
label: core

text: There was no patch, no CVE and no user-facing workaround.
label: core

text: The target was the Grok web chat on grok.com running Grok 4.5 Fast, and Adversa told The Hacker News it had succeeded in 40% of 20 attempts since June (8), with failures caused by Grok struggling to decrypt, not by a filter ( The Hacker News ).
label: core

text: Watch the chain, then switch to the method it replaced, a plain-text injection, and to the defence that holds: Encrypted payload (the attack) Plain-text injection Encrypted, with an egress gate ◀◀ ▶ Play ▶▶ Speed 0.5× 1× 2× The steps and the four private fields are Adversa's account ( write-up ); operational payloads were withheld, so the page text is schematic.
label: fat

text: The plain-text and egress-gate runs are the counterfactuals Adversa's analysis describes, not tests it ran on Grok.
label: core

text: Why encryption, and why it matters.
label: fat

text: Earlier cipher-based evasions used weak, reversible schemes (substitution, XOR, base64) that a model can undo in its weights and a filter can learn to spot.
label: core

text: AES-256-GCM under a PBKDF2-derived key cannot be read by a classifier even with the key on the same page, because recovering the plaintext means running the cipher, and classifiers do not execute what they inspect ( Adversa AI ).
label: core

text: The decryption happens in Grok's own Python runtime, inside the trust boundary, after every filter has passed the request.
label: core

text: It is the clearest demonstration that input filtering cannot secure a model allowed to execute code.
label: core

text: The transferable lessons, that a sandboxed interpreter is an injection decoder and that egress control and action-keyed confirmation are the controls that hold, are on Harness engineering .
label: core
